newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Leighton sells mesh unit for A$140 mln.
newsitem.headline: Leighton sells mesh unit for A$140 mln.

text.p: Construction and civil engineering group Leighton Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it had sold the business and assets of its Welded Mesh Pty Ltd subsidiary to Smorgon Steel Pty Ltd for A$140 million.
Leighton said it expected the sale would generate an after-tax abnormal profit of about A$48 million.
Leighton, Australia's largest construction group, said proceeds of the sale would be used to further develop the core businesses of the Leighton group.
Leighton said Weld Mesh was Australia's third largest manufacturer and supplier of steel reinforcing mesh, bar and rod, hard drawn wire and allied products.
Leighton chief executive Wal King said that in a very competitive market, Welded Mesh was at a stage where stronger links to a steel manufacturer were essential for further growth.
"At a time when we were reviewing the company's long term strategy, Smorgon Steel made an attractive offer for the business," King said in a statement.
The sale was expected to be completed within three months, subject to there being no objection from the anti-monopolies authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
Smorgon Steel is a major privately-owned integrated steel producer.
Leighton shares were two cents firmer at A$5.21 at 3.40 p.m. (0540 GMT).
